caption: the original egyptian marble line - winged Isis, rolling chains and the gap shot that challenged zuma.
about: Luxor (2004) is the game that turned the marble-shooter wave into a genre of its own: a winged shooter slides along the bottom of the screen while ball chains wind through egyptian temple tracks, and matching three destroys them. Power balls - scatter shot, lightning, reverse, slow - fall from destroyed groups, and the line between survival and a wiped chain is always one missed gap shot.

The original pc build is gone from the current stores, carried today by archive routes. The series it started ran six mainline windows entries, and every one of them keeps the same laws this first game wrote.
